target_customer: Academic and enterprise life science labs and biotech and pharma companies analysing microscopy images
problem: Microscopy image analysis took months of scripting and infrastructure work. Biodock offers no code AI training and analysis in the cloud.
business_model: SaaS subscription for cloud image analysis with usage and compute

founders.name: Nurlybek Mursaliyev
education: Stanford University, PhD in cell and molecular biology
previous_startups: SmartLens (contact lens for intraocular pressure; left to focus on PhD)
founders.background_notes: YC page and a January 2026 Digital Business interview. A second Stanford co-founder is mentioned but not named in sources opened.

competitors.name: Aivia (DRVision)
competitors.what: AI microscopy image analysis with a cloud platform

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed deep learning models for varied biological images, GPU compute that scales, and multichannel image handling with a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Workflow and trained model lock in is modest. Open source tools and larger microscope vendors offered substitutes.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Microscope vendors kept building their own cloud AI tools. No acquisition of Biodock found in news searches through November 2026.

market_need_then: Imaging labs generated large volumes of microscopy data and lacked ML staff. The founder describes the problem from his own Stanford research.

branding.domain_note: Now at biodock.ai; earlier domain not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, speed and accessibility focused: deep AI for biological images, no code

branding.community_and_virality: A founder podcast on nFactorial and local Kazakh press coverage exist.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear descriptive name suggesting biology plus a platform, but little evidence of brand driven growth. Company claims over 5,000 labs.

pivots.from: Scientific project funded by an NSF grant and StartX
pivots.to: AI to speed up microscopy image analysis
pivots.why: Per founder interview, the team settled on AI image analysis after trying other ideas. Dates not stated.

outcome_analysis: Biodock took an early round of about 2.2 million dollars led by a16z around YC W21 and says total funding is 3.8 million dollars, a small amount over five years. It reports over 5,000 labs as users and holds SOC2 Type II. Growth looks steady and capital efficient rather than venture scale, with limited public data.
notes: Funding is inconsistent across aggregators (CB Insights, PremierALTS, SeedTable). An aggregator listed a 3.8 million dollar seed dated Nov 2025, but the January 2026 interview describes 3.8 million as total raised, so not recorded as a round. A 100 thousand dollar grant on 2022-01-06 appears only on CB Insights, unverified. The interview gives no month for the 2.2 million round; March 2021 comes from an aggregator and the YC batch timing. Aivia Cloud date is from a search summary of the vendor release. arivis Cloud (formerly APEER) not listed because no dated source was opened.
